category: Mathematics interfaces (PDE, classical PDEs, ODE/DAE, Events, curvilinear, deformed meshes, extra dimensions) and COMSOL add-ins
description: Core COMSOL Multiphysics equation-based modeling beyond the basic PDE entries: lower-dimensional PDE interfaces, the Classical PDE interfaces (Laplace, Poisson, Helmholtz, heat, wave, convection-diffusion, stabilized convection-diffusion), PDE boundary elements, edge/point ODEs, distributed ODE and algebraic equation nodes, the Events interface nodes, PDE boundary and domain conditions, auxiliary equation-based nodes, Wave Form PDE interior conditions, Wall Distance and Curvilinear Coordinates methods, deformed-mesh (Deforming Domain) conditions, extra dimensions, and the add-ins shipped in the Add-in Libraries. Type strings verified against the COMSOL 6.4 completion data.

tools.name: Coefficient Form Boundary PDE (cb) / Edge PDE (ce) / Point PDE (cp)
tools.description: Lower-dimensional variants of the Coefficient Form PDE that solve equations whose dependent variables live only on boundaries (surfaces in 3D), edges or points, with tangential derivatives, for thin-film, membrane-transport, surface-reaction or cable-type models coupled to the surrounding domain physics. Settings and coefficients (c, a, f, ea, da, alpha, beta, gamma) are the same as for the domain Coefficient Form PDE.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Mathematics > PDE Interfaces > Lower Dimensions > Coefficient Form Boundary PDE / Edge PDE / Point PDE; API: physics().create("cb", "CoefficientFormBoundaryPDE", "geom1"); create("ce", "CoefficientFormEdgePDE", "geom1"); create("cp", "CoefficientFormPointPDE", "geom1")

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Boundaries, edges or points on which the variable is defined.

parameters.name: Coefficients
parameters.description: c, a, f, ea, da, alpha, beta, gamma as in Coefficient Form PDE (with tangential derivatives).

parameters.name: Units / Discretization
parameters.description: Dependent-variable and source quantities; shape function order.

tools.notes: Couple to domain variables directly in expressions (the domain variable is evaluated on the boundary). The existing 'Coefficient Form PDE (c)' entry covers the domain interface.

tools.name: General Form Boundary PDE (gb) / Edge PDE (ge) / Point PDE (gp)
tools.description: Lower-dimensional General Form PDE interfaces where the flux vector Gamma and source f are arbitrary (nonlinear) expressions of the dependent variable and its tangential derivatives on boundaries, edges or points. They suit nonlinear surface transport, shell-like equations written in conservative form and 1D line equations embedded in 3D.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Mathematics > PDE Interfaces > Lower Dimensions > General Form Boundary/Edge/Point PDE; API: physics().create("gb", "GeneralFormBoundaryPDE", "geom1"); create("ge", "GeneralFormEdgePDE", "geom1"); create("gp", "GeneralFormPointPDE", "geom1")

parameters.name: Gamma (Ga) / f / da / ea
parameters.description: Conservative flux, source, damping and mass coefficients.

tools.notes: Note that the default name ge for General Form Edge PDE is the same as for Global ODEs and DAEs; COMSOL appends numbers when both are present.

tools.name: Weak Form Boundary PDE (wb) / Edge PDE (we) / Point PDE (wp)
tools.description: Weak-form equation interfaces restricted to boundaries, edges or points, where the full weak expression is written with test() functions and tangential derivative operators (dtang, or variable names with T suffix). They are the most flexible way to implement custom surface physics such as shells, thin films or Lagrange-multiplier fields on boundaries.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Mathematics > PDE Interfaces > Lower Dimensions > Weak Form Boundary/Edge/Point PDE; API: physics().create("wb", "WeakFormBoundaryPDE", "geom1"); create("we", "WeakFormEdgePDE", "geom1"); create("wp", "WeakFormPointPDE", "geom1")

parameters.name: weak
parameters.description: Weak expression (sum of terms containing test functions).

parameters.name: Discretization
parameters.description: Shape function type and order of the boundary variable.

tools.notes: Tangential derivatives are available as uTx, uTy, uTz for boundary variables.

tools.name: Laplace's Equation (lpeq)
tools.description: Classical PDE interface for -div(grad u) = 0 (elliptic), e.g. potentials, steady diffusion without sources or harmonic extensions. It is a preset Coefficient Form PDE with only the diffusion term; the same equation can also be added as a domain node in any PDE interface.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Mathematics > Classical PDEs > Laplace's Equation; API: physics().create("lpeq", "LaplaceEquation", "geom1") (domain node type LaplaceEquation, tag leq1)

parameters.name: Boundary conditions
parameters.description: Dirichlet Boundary Condition, Flux/Source, Zero Flux (default), Periodic Condition.

tools.notes: Classical PDE interfaces (except Stabilized Convection-Diffusion) are not available in axisymmetric components; use Coefficient Form PDE with the r factors instead.

tools.name: Poisson's Equation (poeq)
tools.description: Classical elliptic PDE -div(c grad u) = f, for example electrostatics with space charge, steady heat conduction with sources, or torsion stress functions. It exposes only the diffusion coefficient c and source f of the Coefficient Form PDE.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Mathematics > Classical PDEs > Poisson's Equation; API: physics().create("poeq", "PoissonEquation", "geom1"); domain node PoissonEquation (peq1) with c and f

parameters.name: c
parameters.description: Diffusion coefficient (scalar, diagonal, symmetric or full).

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: Source term.

tools.notes: Physical units can be set in the interface Units section so that c and f carry units.

tools.name: Helmholtz Equation (hzeq)
tools.description: Classical elliptic PDE -div(c grad u) + a u = f, the time-harmonic form of the wave equation (a = -k^2 for waves) or a screened Poisson equation (a > 0) used for example for Helmholtz filters. Solve it with a Stationary study or as an eigenvalue problem.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Mathematics > Classical PDEs > Helmholtz Equation; API: physics().create("hzeq", "HelmholtzEquation", "geom1"); domain node HelmholtzEquation (heq1) with c, a, f

parameters.name: c
parameters.description: Diffusion coefficient.

parameters.name: a
parameters.description: Absorption coefficient (negative k^2 for propagating waves).

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: Source term.

tools.notes: For acoustics or electromagnetics prefer the dedicated physics interfaces (radiation conditions, PMLs, ports).

tools.name: Heat Equation (hteq)
tools.description: Classical parabolic PDE da du/dt - div(c grad u) = f for transient diffusion processes (heat conduction or any linear diffusion) in dimensionless or user-chosen units. Use it for quick equation-based diffusion problems or as a template for coupled custom physics.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Mathematics > Classical PDEs > Heat Equation; API: physics().create("hteq", "HeatEquation", "geom1"); domain node HeatEquation (hteq1) with da, c, f

parameters.name: da
parameters.description: Damping (mass) coefficient, e.g. rho*Cp.

parameters.name: c
parameters.description: Diffusion coefficient, e.g. k.

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: Source term.

tools.notes: Not to be confused with the Heat Transfer interfaces, which add convection, radiation, materials and heat-specific boundary conditions.

tools.name: Wave Equation (waeq)
tools.description: Classical hyperbolic PDE ea d2u/dt2 - div(c grad u) = f for transient scalar waves (sound, strings, membranes) solved with an implicit time-dependent solver; initial values need both u and du/dt. For large explicit wave problems use the Wave Form PDE (discontinuous Galerkin) interface instead.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Mathematics > Classical PDEs > Wave Equation; API: physics().create("waeq", "WaveEquation", "geom1"); domain node WaveEquation (weq1) with ea, c, f

parameters.name: ea
parameters.description: Mass coefficient (1/c0^2 scaling).

parameters.name: c
parameters.description: Diffusion coefficient (wave speed squared times ea).

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: Source term.

tools.notes: Resolve the wavelength with about 5-10 second-order elements and limit time steps accordingly (generalized-alpha works well).

tools.name: Convection-Diffusion Equation (cdeq)
tools.description: Classical PDE da du/dt - div(c grad u) + beta . grad u = f for transport of a scalar by a velocity field with diffusion, without the stabilization of the dedicated physics interfaces. Suitable for diffusion-dominated or well-resolved problems; for high Peclet numbers use the Stabilized Convection-Diffusion Equation.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Mathematics > Classical PDEs > Convection-Diffusion Equation; API: physics().create("cdeq", "ConvectionDiffusionEquation", "geom1"); domain node ConvectionDiffusionEquation (cdeq1) with da, c, be, f

parameters.name: da / c / f
parameters.description: Mass coefficient, diffusion coefficient and source.

parameters.name: be
parameters.description: Convection coefficient vector beta (velocity).

tools.notes: Unstabilized Galerkin discretization oscillates when the cell Peclet number exceeds about 1.

tools.name: Stabilized Convection-Diffusion Equation (scdeq)
tools.description: Classical convection-diffusion interface with numerical stabilization for convection-dominated transport: streamline diffusion and crosswind diffusion (consistent stabilization, on by default) and optional isotropic diffusion (inconsistent). It also offers transport-style boundary conditions (No Flux, No Diffusive Flux, Flux/Source, Interior Dirichlet, Line and Point Sources) and, unlike the other classical PDEs, works in 2D axisymmetry.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Mathematics > Classical PDEs > Stabilized Convection-Diffusion Equation; API: physics().create("scdeq", "StabilizedConvectionDiffusionEquation", "geom1")

parameters.name: Consistent Stabilization
parameters.description: Streamline diffusion and crosswind diffusion (default on).

parameters.name: Inconsistent Stabilization
parameters.description: Isotropic diffusion (off by default).

parameters.name: Boundary nodes
parameters.description: NoFlux, NoDiffusiveFlux, FluxSource, InteriorDirichletBoundaryCondition (ru/rd), LineSource, PointSource, PeriodicCondition.

tools.notes: Cannot be combined with other PDE forms in the same interface.

tools.name: PDE, Boundary Elements (pdebe)
tools.description: Boundary element method interface for Laplace/Poisson-type equations (-div(c grad u) + a u, fundamental-solution based) that meshes only boundaries and can model domains, finite voids and an infinite void without truncating the exterior. It can be coupled to FEM physics on shared boundaries and is well suited to open-domain potential problems.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Mathematics > PDE Interfaces > PDE, Boundary Elements; API: physics().create("pdebe", "PDEBoundaryElements", "geom1"); domain node PDEBoundaryElements (bem1); boundary DirichletBC (bdir), Flux (bflux), ZeroFlux (zflx)

parameters.name: c / a
parameters.description: Diffusion and absorption coefficients of the BEM domain.

parameters.name: Infinite void / finite voids
parameters.description: Region types handled without volume mesh.

parameters.name: Far-field condition / operator
parameters.description: Behavior at infinity (bemOperator name for evaluation).

tools.notes: BEM produces dense matrices; iterative solvers with compressed (ACA+) assembly keep memory manageable. Postprocess in space with Grid datasets that evaluate the BEM solution.

tools.name: Edge ODEs and DAEs (eode) / Point ODEs and DAEs (pode)
tools.description: Distributed ODE interfaces whose dependent variables are defined on edges or points and have no spatial derivatives: each node solves ea d2u/dt2 + da du/dt = f locally, for example damage or state variables along welds, wire temperatures or lumped states at probe points. They complement the Domain and Boundary ODE interfaces.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Mathematics > ODE and DAE Interfaces > Edge ODEs and DAEs / Point ODEs and DAEs; API: physics().create("eode", "EdgeODE", "geom1"); physics().create("pode", "PointODE", "geom1")

parameters.name: Distributed ODE (ea, da, f)
parameters.description: Default equation node.

parameters.name: Algebraic Equation
parameters.description: Alternative node for f = 0 constraints.

parameters.name: Units
parameters.description: Dependent-variable and source-term quantities.

tools.notes: Existing entry 'Boundary ODEs and DAEs (bode) / Domain ODEs and DAEs (dode)' covers the domain/boundary variants.

tools.name: Distributed ODE / Algebraic Equation (ODE and DAE interfaces)
tools.description: Equation nodes of the distributed ODE/DAE interfaces: Distributed ODE (default) solves ea utt + da ut = f pointwise, and Algebraic Equation enforces f = 0 for each dependent variable, turning the system into a DAE (for example a local equilibrium or a constitutive state update). Both can be mixed on different selections.
tools.usage: Domain/Boundary/Edge/Point ODEs and DAEs > Distributed ODE (dode1) or Algebraic Equation (aleq1); API: physics("dode").create("aleq1", "AlgebraicEquation", 3)

parameters.name: ea / da / f (Distributed ODE)
parameters.description: Mass, damping and source coefficients.

parameters.name: f (Algebraic Equation)
parameters.description: Expression that is driven to zero.

tools.notes: Distributed ODE variables use Lagrange or discontinuous shape functions; choose discontinuous for history variables in Gauss points.

tools.name: Discrete States / Indicator States (Events interface)
tools.description: Events interface nodes defining state variables: Discrete States are piecewise-constant globals (with initial values) changed only by events, used as switches in equations (heater on/off, valve open); Indicator States are continuous states computed from g-expressions whose zero crossings the time-dependent solver locates accurately to trigger Implicit Events. Together they implement hybrid (switched) dynamics such as thermostats and relays.
tools.usage: Events (ev) > Discrete States (ds1) / Indicator States (is1); API: physics("ev").create("ds1", "DiscreteStates", -1); create("is1", "IndicatorStates", -1)

parameters.name: dim / dimInit / dimDescr (Discrete States)
parameters.description: Name, initial value and description of each discrete state.

parameters.name: indDim / g / dimInit (Indicator States)
parameters.description: Indicator name, g-coefficient expression and initial value.

tools.notes: Indicator expressions must not contain other indicator states; they are wrapped in nojac() to avoid Jacobian fill-in.

tools.name: Explicit Event / Explicit Event List (Events interface)
tools.description: Events at predefined times: an Explicit Event fires at a start time and optionally periodically, stopping the solver and reinitializing global states (and, via subnodes, domain/boundary/edge/point variables); an Explicit Event List defines its own discrete state that is set to a new value at each time in a table, ideal for multi-step load programs. Reinitialization subnodes can also reset field variables when the event fires.
tools.usage: Events (ev) > Explicit Event (expl1) / Explicit Event List (expll1); API: physics("ev").create("expl1", "ExplicitEvent", -1); create("expll1", "ExplicitEventList", -1)

parameters.name: start / period (Explicit Event)
parameters.description: First event time and repetition period.

parameters.name: reInitName / reInitValue
parameters.description: Variables and reinitialization expressions.

parameters.name: variableName / initialValue / time / reinitializationExpression (List)
parameters.description: Discrete state and its value table.

parameters.name: useConsistentInit / ignoreIdenticalConsecutive
parameters.description: Consistent reinitialization; skip events with unchanged value.

tools.notes: Events force the time stepper to hit the event times exactly and restart, which keeps discontinuous loads accurate.

tools.name: Implicit Event (Events interface)
tools.description: Event triggered when a condition on indicator states (using <, >, !, ||, &&) switches from false to true at a zero crossing located by the solver, after which global states or field variables are reinitialized. Typical uses are thermostats, bouncing contact switches, and stopping a process when a threshold is reached.
tools.usage: Events (ev) > Implicit Event (impl1); API: physics("ev").create("impl1", "ImplicitEvent", -1); set("condition", "Tup>0")

parameters.name: condition
parameters.description: Logical condition on indicator states, e.g. z>0 (z>1 never triggers).

parameters.name: reInitName / reInitValue
parameters.description: Global variables to reinitialize.

parameters.name: useConsistentInit
parameters.description: Correct dependent variables after reinitialization (default on).

tools.notes: Only zero crossings of indicator states are detected, so write conditions as 'indicator compared to 0'.

tools.name: Event Sequence / Sequence Member (Events interface)
tools.description: Builds an ordered sequence of process stages without manually wiring explicit and implicit events: each Sequence Member sets a discrete state and ends after a duration or when an end-condition expression becomes positive, with optional reinitializations; the sequence can loop throughout the study. Suitable for charge/discharge cycles, batch process recipes and test protocols.
tools.usage: Events (ev) > Event Sequence (es1) > Sequence Member (sm1, sm2, ...); API: physics("ev").create("es1", "EventSequence", -1); feature("es1").create("sm1", "SequenceMember", -1)

parameters.name: loop
parameters.description: Repeat the sequence.

parameters.name: stateName
parameters.description: Discrete state name controlled by the member.

parameters.name: endConditionOptions / duration / condition
parameters.description: End by duration or by expression > 0.

parameters.name: reInitName / reInitValue
parameters.description: Reinitializations when the member starts.

tools.notes: Each member's discrete state is 1 while that member is active, making it easy to switch boundary conditions.

tools.name: Reinitialization on Domains, Boundaries, Edges, or Points (Events interface)
tools.description: Subnodes of Explicit and Implicit Event that reinitialize field dependent variables on selected geometric entities when the event fires, for example resetting a concentration after a flushing step or a temperature after a quench. After all reinitializations the solver optionally enforces consistency with a small backward-Euler step.
tools.usage: Right-click Explicit Event / Implicit Event > Reinitialization on Domains | Boundaries | Edges | Points; API: feature("impl1").create("reinit1", "ReinitDomain", 3) (ReinitBoundary, ReinitEdge, ReinitPoint)

parameters.name: reInitName / reInitValue
parameters.description: Dependent variables and new values or expressions.

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Entities where the reinitialization applies.

tools.notes: Clear 'Use consistent initialization' only when the reinitialized state is already consistent, to save time.

tools.name: Dirichlet Boundary Condition / Constraint (PDE interfaces)
tools.description: Boundary conditions of the PDE interfaces that prescribe values: Dirichlet Boundary Condition sets u = r per dependent variable (with elemental or nodal, pointwise or weak constraints and choice of reaction-term symmetry), while Constraint enforces a general bidirectional expression R = 0. Excluded Points/Edges subnodes remove the constraint from bounding entities.
tools.usage: PDE interface > Dirichlet Boundary Condition (dir1) / Constraint (cons1); API: physics("c").create("dir1", "DirichletBoundary", 2); create("cons1", "Constraint", 2)

parameters.name: r / useDirichletCondition
parameters.description: Prescribed value per variable and whether it is active.

parameters.name: R (Constraint)
parameters.description: Constraint expression set to zero.

parameters.name: constraintType
parameters.description: symmetricConstraint | unidirectionalVar | unidirectionalConstraint reaction-term handling.

parameters.name: constraintMethod / weakConstraints
parameters.description: elemental | nodal; pointwise or weak (Lagrange multiplier) constraints.

tools.notes: Weak constraints make the reaction flux available as a Lagrange multiplier variable but add degrees of freedom.

tools.name: Flux/Source / Zero Flux / No Flux (PDE interfaces)
tools.description: Natural (Neumann/Robin) boundary conditions of PDE interfaces: Flux/Source adds -n.Gamma = g - q u (boundary source g and absorption/impedance q), Zero Flux is the default homogeneous Neumann condition, and No Flux / No Diffusive Flux are the transport-flavored equivalents in the stabilized convection-diffusion interface. Setting q = h and g = h*T_ext gives a Robin (convective) condition.
tools.usage: PDE interface > Flux/Source (flux1), Zero Flux (default zflx1); API: physics("c").create("flux1", "FluxBoundary", 2); set("g", ...), set("q", ...)

parameters.name: g
parameters.description: Boundary flux/source.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Boundary absorption/impedance term (Robin condition).

tools.notes: Interior Flux/Source applies the same on interior boundaries.

tools.name: Source / Edge Source / Point Source / Line Source (PDE interfaces)
tools.description: Additional source contributions of PDE interfaces: Source adds f on domains, Edge Source adds a line source on 3D edges, Point Source adds a concentrated source at points, and Line Source (stabilized convection-diffusion) adds sources along lines. They let you superpose sources without editing the main equation node.
tools.usage: PDE interface > Source (src1) / Edge Source (edgsrc1) / Point Source (ptsrc1); API: physics("c").create("src1", "SourceTerm", 3); create("edgsrc1", "EdgeSourceTerm", 1); create("ptsrc1", "PointSourceTerm", 0)

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: Source strength (per volume, length or point).

tools.notes: Point and edge sources create singular solutions; evaluate integral quantities rather than point values nearby.

tools.name: Periodic Condition (PDE interfaces)
tools.description: Maps the solution between source and destination boundaries of PDE interfaces with Continuity or Antiperiodicity, automatic or user-defined transformation to an intermediate map, optional elementwise mapping for compatible (copied) meshes, and elemental or nodal constraints. Use it for unit cells and repeating geometries in equation-based models.
tools.usage: PDE interface > Periodic Condition (pc1); API: physics("c").create("pc1", "PeriodicCondition", 2); set("PeriodicType", "Continuity"|"AntiPeriodicity")

parameters.name: PeriodicType
parameters.description: Continuity | AntiPeriodicity.

parameters.name: TransformationMethod
parameters.description: automatic | GlobalSystem (intermediate map).

parameters.name: meshSimilarity / meshSimilarityTol
parameters.description: Elementwise mapping for compatible meshes (def, auto, off, fail).

parameters.name: Destination Selection (manual)
parameters.description: Right-click > Manual Destination Selection when automatic pairing fails.

tools.notes: Copy the mesh from source to destination (Copy Face / Copy Edge) for the most accurate periodic mapping.

tools.name: Prescribed Solution / Excluded Points, Edges, Surfaces (PDE interfaces)
tools.description: Prescribed Solution is a domain-level Dirichlet condition that fixes u on whole domains, overriding the PDE there (useful for inactive regions or known fields). Excluded Points, Edges and Surfaces subnodes of Constraint, Dirichlet Boundary Condition, Pointwise Constraint and Prescribed Solution remove the constraint from bounding entities where it would conflict with adjacent physics.
tools.usage: PDE interface > More > Prescribed Solution (prs1); right-click a constraint node > Excluded Points / Excluded Edges / Excluded Surfaces; API: physics("c").create("prs1", "PrescribedSolution", 3); feature("dir1").create("excl1", "ExcludedEdges", 1)

parameters.name: r / useDirichletCondition
parameters.description: Prescribed value per variable.

parameters.name: Excluded selection
parameters.description: Points, edges or surfaces to leave unconstrained.

tools.notes: Excluding shared edges avoids over-constraining when two different Dirichlet values meet.

tools.name: Auxiliary Dependent Variable (Weak Contribution subnode)
tools.description: Subnode of Weak Contribution or Weak Contribution on Mesh Boundaries that declares an extra dependent variable (field variable name, initial value and time derivative, shape function and order) used in a weak expression that is not part of the physics interface. It is how Lagrange multipliers, extra fields for custom constitutive laws or mixed formulations are added to any physics.
tools.usage: Show More Options > Equation-Based Contributions; right-click Weak Contribution > Auxiliary Dependent Variable (aux1); API: physics("ht").feature("weak1").create("aux1", "AuxiliaryField", 3)

parameters.name: fieldVariableName / initialValue / initialTimeDerivative
parameters.description: Variable definition and initial conditions.

parameters.name: shapeFunctionType / order / frame
parameters.description: Discretization (Lagrange, discontinuous, bubble, ...) and frame.

parameters.name: valueType
parameters.description: real | complex when splitting complex variables.

tools.notes: The existing 'Weak Contribution / Weak Constraint / Pointwise Constraint / Global Constraint' entry describes the parent nodes.

tools.name: Weak Inequality Constraint
tools.description: Equation-based node that enforces an inequality constraint m <= 0 with a complementary Lagrange multiplier (reaction) that is nonzero only where the constraint is active, using a penalty or augmented Lagrangian method on domains, boundaries, edges or points of any physics interface. It suits custom contact, obstacle and unilateral problems.
tools.usage: Show More Options > Equation-Based Contributions; right-click physics > More > Weak Inequality Constraint (wic1); API: physics("c").create("wic1", "WeakInequalityConstraint", 2)

parameters.name: constraintExpression
parameters.description: Expression m constrained to be <= 0.

parameters.name: method / ks
parameters.description: penalty | augmentedLagrangian and spring constant.

parameters.name: useDt / dt
parameters.description: Optional transition zone for smoother activation.

parameters.name: constraintType / constraintForce
parameters.description: Reaction terms on all physics (symmetric) or user-defined force expression.

tools.notes: No global variant exists. Strongly nonlinear: use a segregated or damped Newton solver and ramp the penalty.

tools.name: Weak Contribution on Mesh Boundaries
tools.description: Domain-level equation-based node whose weak expression is applied on every interior mesh element boundary (faces in 3D, edges in 2D) of the selected domains, with up() and down() giving values on each side. Combined with discontinuous shape functions it implements discontinuous Galerkin fluxes and interior penalty terms.
tools.usage: Show More Options > Equation-Based Contributions; right-click physics > More > Weak Contribution on Mesh Boundaries (ibweak1); API: physics("w").create("ibweak1", "InteriorBoundaryContribution", 3)

parameters.name: weakExpression
parameters.description: Weak form using up(u), down(u), test() and the mesh normal.

parameters.name: integrationOrder / quadratureFrame
parameters.description: Quadrature settings.

parameters.name: Auxiliary Dependent Variable subnode
parameters.description: Extra field used in the expression.

tools.notes: Element faces that are real geometry boundaries are not included.

tools.name: Discretization (node) - multiple discretizations per physics
tools.description: Global node (Advanced Physics Options) that adds alternative discretizations (shape function types and orders) to a physics interface; study steps and Multigrid Level nodes can then select which discretization to use, for example to compare linear and quadratic elements or to build a manual p-multigrid hierarchy. The node only appears when Advanced Physics Options are enabled.
tools.usage: Show More Options > Advanced Physics Options; right-click the physics interface > Global > Discretization (disc1); select it in Study step > Physics and Variables Selection > Discretization; API: physics("c").create("disc1", "Discretization", -1); set("shapeorder", "1")

parameters.name: shapeorder / shapeorderExpr
parameters.description: Element order (Linear ... Quintic) or expression.

tools.notes: Useful for convergence studies without duplicating the model.

tools.name: Interior Flux / Interior Flux Split / Interior Source (Wave Form PDE)
tools.description: Interior-boundary conditions of the time-explicit discontinuous-Galerkin Wave Form PDE: Interior Flux prescribes the numerical flux on an interior boundary, Interior Flux Split specifies separate downside and upside fluxes (gd, gu) for one-sided or transmitting conditions, and Interior Source injects waves from an interior surface. Local time stepping (third-order Adams-Bashforth per element group) avoids CFL limits set by a few small elements.
tools.usage: Wave Form PDE (wahw) > Interior Flux / Interior Flux Split / Interior Source; time stepping settings in the Time Explicit solver

parameters.name: gd / gu (Interior Flux Split)
parameters.description: Downside and upside flux terms.

parameters.name: Local time stepping
parameters.description: Groups elements by size so each group uses its own stable step.

tools.example: Wave Form PDE for a 2D scalar wave: add Interior Source on an internal line to emit a Gaussian pulse and Interior Flux Split with gu = 0 on a second line to model a one-way absorbing screen; solve with the Time Explicit solver and local time stepping on a graded mesh.
tools.notes: Only interior boundaries can be selected. The existing 'Wave Form PDE (wahw)' entry covers the interface itself.

tools.name: Distance Equation / Wall Distance Continuity (Wall Distance interface)
tools.description: Nodes of the Wall Distance interface: Distance Equation (default domain node) solves the modified eikonal equation giving the reciprocal wall distance field used by turbulence models and other distance-dependent expressions, and Wall Distance Continuity keeps the distance continuous across identity, contact or sector pair boundaries instead of treating them as walls. Periodic Condition handles periodic domains.
tools.usage: Wall Distance (wd) > Distance Equation (deq1), Wall (wall1), Wall Distance Continuity (pair), Periodic Condition; API: physics("wd").create("pwdc1", "PeriodicWallDistanceCondition", 2)

parameters.name: Reference length scale (interface)
parameters.description: Controls the accuracy far from walls.

parameters.name: Pairs
parameters.description: Pair boundaries across which the distance is continuous.

tools.example: Assembly with a rotating domain: add Wall Distance Continuity on the identity pair between rotor and stator so the turbulence model sees a continuous wall distance; solve with Study > Wall Distance Initialization.
tools.notes: The existing 'Wall Distance (wd)' and 'Wall Distance Initialization' entries cover the interface and the study step.

tools.name: Diffusion / Elasticity / Flow / Adaptive Method (Curvilinear Coordinates)
tools.description: Methods of the Curvilinear Coordinates interface for computing a smooth vector field that defines local fiber or winding directions: Diffusion (Laplace potential, good for smooth geometries), Elasticity (eigenvalue-based, needs an eigenvalue study), Flow (Stokes-flow field for varying cross sections) and Adaptive (constant streamline density per cross section, similar to coil geometry analysis), plus a User Defined option. The result creates a Curvilinear System for anisotropic materials.
tools.usage: Curvilinear Coordinates (cc) > Diffusion Method (diff1) / Elasticity Method (elas1) / Flow Method (flow1) / Adaptive Method (adap1) / User Defined; API: physics("cc").create("flow1", "FlowMethod", 3)

parameters.name: Method subnodes
parameters.description: Inlet, Outlet, Wall (default), Interior Wall, Jump depending on method.

parameters.name: Normalize vector field (interface)
parameters.description: Unit vectors or conserved field magnitude.

parameters.name: Coordinate System Settings
parameters.description: Second basis vector (x, y, z or user defined) of the generated system.

tools.notes: Use a Jump node for closed-loop fields (tori, coils); the Elasticity method needs an eigenvalue study step.

tools.name: Attached Dimensions / Average and Integration Over Extra Dimension
tools.description: Extra-dimension framework for problems where each point of a base geometry carries its own additional space, such as diffusion inside particles of a porous electrode or through-thickness fields: Attached Dimensions forms the Cartesian product of a base selection with one or more Extra Dimension geometries, and Average/Integration Over Extra Dimension operators couple the product geometry back to the base. This avoids meshing the full high-dimensional geometry explicitly.
tools.usage: Global Definitions > Extra Dimension (geometry); base Component > Definitions > Extra Dimensions > Attached Dimensions; Extra Dimension > Definitions > Extra Dimensions > Average / Integration Over Extra Dimension

parameters.name: Geometric entity level / Extra dimensions to attach
parameters.description: Base selection and list of extra dimensions.

parameters.name: Operator name / Source selection
parameters.description: Name and selection of the average or integration operator.

parameters.name: Integration order / Frame / Compute integral in revolved geometry
parameters.description: Quadrature settings.

tools.example: Reference Manual example 'Solving Poisson's Equation in a Cylinder by Means of Extra Dimensions': a 1D base line with an attached 2D disc extra dimension reproduces a 3D cylinder solution.
tools.notes: Physics in the product geometry uses the base selection for its domain; mesh the extra dimension separately.

tools.name: Deforming Domain and mesh smoothing methods (Laplace, Winslow, Hyperelastic, Yeoh)
tools.description: Deformed Geometry / Moving Mesh Definitions feature that lets the mesh inside selected domains follow boundary motion, controlled by a smoothing equation: Laplace, Winslow, Hyperelastic or Yeoh (default, with stiffening factor C2), with linear or logarithmic volumetric strain and optional HuHu or HuHu-LuLu stabilization for higher-order geometry shape functions. Boundary shapes come from explicit conditions or from continuity with adjacent domains.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Moving Mesh (or Deformed Geometry) > Deforming Domain; API: model.component("comp1").common().create("free1", "DeformingDomain") (DeformingDomainDeformedGeometry for Deformed Geometry)

parameters.name: Mesh smoothing type
parameters.description: Laplace | Winslow | Hyperelastic | Yeoh (default).

parameters.name: Stiffening factor C2 / Volumetric strain
parameters.description: Yeoh nonlinearity; Linear or Logarithmic strain measure.

parameters.name: Stabilization / Tuning parameter
parameters.description: None | HuHu | HuHu-LuLu.

parameters.name: Initial deformation
parameters.description: Starting displacement of the domain.

tools.notes: Winslow and Yeoh tolerate larger deformations than Laplace; combine with Automatic Remeshing when elements invert. See also 'Deformed Geometry (dg) vs Moving Mesh (ale)'.

tools.name: Mesh Slip / Rotating Boundary / Prescribed Normal Mesh Velocity (deforming-domain boundary conditions)
tools.description: Boundary conditions for Deforming Domains: Mesh Slip lets mesh nodes slide tangentially (zero normal velocity), Rotating Boundary makes a boundary rotate with a user-defined angle, constant or general angular velocity, or revolutions per time, and Prescribed Normal Mesh Velocity moves a boundary with a given normal speed (e.g. etching, melting, growth) with optional moving-boundary smoothing based on mean curvature.
tools.usage: Component > Definitions > Moving Mesh / Deformed Geometry > Mesh Slip (slip1) / Rotating Boundary (rotb1) / Prescribed Normal Mesh Velocity (pnmv1); API types Slip, RotatingBoundary, PrescribedNormalMeshVelocity (suffix DeformedGeometry for the Deformed Geometry variants)

parameters.name: Normal mesh velocity vn / Enable moving boundary smoothing
parameters.description: Speed and smoothing tuning parameter (default 0.5).

parameters.name: Rotation type
parameters.description: User defined angle | Specified rotational velocity (constant, general, revolutions per time).

parameters.name: Constraint settings
parameters.description: Weak constraints (default) or Nitsche method.

tools.notes: Prescribed Normal Mesh Velocity is intended for Time Dependent studies only.

tools.name: Circuit Extractor (add-in)
tools.description: AC/DC Module add-in that converts lumped matrices from Stationary or Frequency Domain Source Sweeps (Electric Currents, Electrostatics, Electrostatics BEM, Magnetic Fields Currents Only, Magnetic and Electric Fields) into an equivalent circuit in the Electrical Circuit interface and a SPICE netlist. Equivalent circuit analogies are R only, L only, C only, R and L, R and C, R-L-C, or impedances Z.
tools.usage: Developer > Add-in Libraries > ACDC_Module > circuit_extractor; Developer > Add-ins > Circuit Extractor > Generate Matrix Input > choose Equivalent Circuit and Evaluation Group > Extract Circuit

parameters.name: Equivalent Circuit
parameters.description: Resistors R only, Inductors L only, Capacitors C only, R and L, R and C, R L and C, Impedances Z.

parameters.name: Lumped quantities
parameters.description: Matrices (evaluation groups) used for extraction.

parameters.name: Conductor feeding / Close conductors / Keep Electrical Circuit
parameters.description: Source type per conductor, grounding, keep the generated cir interface.

tools.example: Solve a Stationary Source Sweep on a 4-terminal busbar in Electric Currents, run Generate Matrix Input, choose 'Resistors R only' and click Extract Circuit to save busbar.cir for SPICE.
tools.notes: The SPICE preview is shown for all analogies except pure impedances.

tools.name: Colored Selections (add-in)
tools.description: COMSOL Multiphysics add-in that generates one Explicit Selection with a random color for every domain or boundary, grouped under Colored Domain Selections or Colored Boundary Selections, with adjustable tint or shade. It makes complex imported assemblies easy to inspect and to pick selections from.
tools.usage: Developer > Add-in Libraries > COMSOL_Multiphysics > colored_selections; ribbon tab Colored Selections > Select (Domains/Boundaries) > Generate / Clear / Settings (Tone: Tint or Shade, amount 0-1)

parameters.name: Select
parameters.description: Domains or Boundaries.

parameters.name: Tone / Tint / Shade
parameters.description: Brighten (tint) or darken (shade) the random RGB colors.

tools.example: Import a 60-part STEP assembly, Colored Selections > Domains > Generate; each domain now shows a distinct color and has a named selection usable in materials and physics.
tools.notes: Clear removes the selection group chosen in Select.

tools.name: Image to Curve (add-in)
tools.description: COMSOL Multiphysics add-in that turns an imported image into geometry: the image is filtered (blur, sharpen), contoured at an automatic or manual threshold, and the contour is converted into an Interpolation Curve in a 2D geometry or a 3D work plane, scaled to a given image width. Useful for building geometries from photos, micrographs or scanned drawings.
tools.usage: Developer > Add-in Libraries > COMSOL_Multiphysics > image_to_curve; Settings toolbar: Browse > Plot > Filter > Contour > Curve (Reset)

parameters.name: Image width / Positive image
parameters.description: Physical size and negative-image option.

parameters.name: Filter
parameters.description: Gaussian blur (default) and other blur/sharpen filters.

parameters.name: Contour threshold
parameters.description: Automatic or manual intensity level.

parameters.name: Curve tolerance
parameters.description: Interpolation curve fitting tolerance.

tools.example: Load a photo of an I-beam cross section, apply Gaussian blur, Contour, Curve; convert the curve to a solid and extrude to 3D for a swept mesh (as in the add-in documentation).
tools.notes: Preprocess noisy images in an image editor for cleaner contours.

tools.name: Mesh Partition with Ball (add-in)
tools.description: COMSOL Multiphysics add-in that adds a Partition with Ball operation to an imported-mesh sequence using the current Clip Sphere (or an automatic radius of twice the average element size, or a manual radius) centered at the clip sphere or rotation center. It speeds up repair of imported STL/medical meshes by isolating faces with self-intersecting elements for deletion and refilling.
tools.usage: Developer > Add-in Libraries > COMSOL_Multiphysics > mesh_partition_with_ball; Settings: Target mesh, Ball Radius (Automatic | Manual | From Clip Sphere) > Create / Refresh

parameters.name: Mesh
parameters.description: Mesh sequence defining its own geometry (imported mesh), not locked or empty.

parameters.name: Radius
parameters.description: Automatic, Manual or From Clip Sphere.

tools.example: Imported bone STL with intersecting triangles: place a clip sphere around the defect, run the add-in (From Clip Sphere), delete the created face, then Fill Holes before creating geometry from the mesh.
tools.notes: Set the rotation center by middle-clicking or via 'Center at Coordinates' in mesh error nodes.

tools.name: Random Particulate Composite RVE (add-in)
tools.description: COMSOL Multiphysics add-in that creates a geometry part of a representative volume element with spherical inclusions of random positions and sizes (fixed, uniform, normal or log-normal diameters with optional CDF capping) or in a predefined pattern, plus a histogram of the generated size distribution. The RVE feeds material homogenization studies.
tools.usage: Developer > Add-in Libraries > COMSOL_Multiphysics > particulate_composite_random; toolbar: Create Geometry Part / Plot Histogram / Reset All

parameters.name: Cell dimensions
parameters.description: Size of the rectangular cell.

parameters.name: Particle size distribution
parameters.description: Fixed | Uniform | Normal | Log-normal with parameters and CDF caps.

parameters.name: Particle position / Number of particles
parameters.description: Random or patterned placement and count/volume fraction.

tools.example: Generate a 1x1x1 mm cell with 60 log-normally distributed glass spheres, insert the part into a 3D component, and use Cell Periodicity in Solid Mechanics to compute effective elastic properties.
tools.notes: Built-in Part Library RVEs only allow predefined sizes and positions; this add-in removes that restriction.

tools.name: PID Controller Setup (add-in)
tools.description: COMSOL Multiphysics add-in that adds a PID Controller component implementing a PID law in position or velocity form with global equations, driven by a probe as the measured output and producing a control variable to use as an actuator (heater power, inlet velocity, voltage). Options include bias, output limits, integral anti-windup (time constant Tt) and derivative filtering (Tf).
tools.usage: Developer > Add-in Libraries > COMSOL_Multiphysics > pid_controller_setup; Developer > Add-ins > PID Controller Setup: choose Component, Probe (and expression), gains kp/ki/kd, Reference value, limits > Apply

parameters.name: PID controller algorithm
parameters.description: Position (default) or Velocity form.

parameters.name: kp / ki / kd / cset / ubias
parameters.description: Gains, setpoint and bias (kd = 0 gives a PI controller).

parameters.name: Lower/Upper limit (umin, umax)
parameters.description: Actuator saturation.

parameters.name: Enable integral anti-windup (Tt) / Enable filtering of derivative (Tf)
parameters.description: Position-form refinements.

tools.example: Domain Point Probe on the sensor temperature, PID Controller Setup with kp = 50, ki = 5, cset = 330[K], umin = 0, umax = 500[W]; use the reported control variable as the Heat Source power and run a Time Dependent study.
tools.notes: The velocity form needs 'Use output solution for the time operators' in the time-dependent solver and preferably fixed time steps.

tools.name: Planar Cut (add-in)
tools.description: COMSOL Multiphysics add-in that cuts a 3D geometry with an xy-, xz- or yz-plane at the midpoint or a user-defined coordinate and removes the upside or downside, automatically adding the required geometry steps. It is a fast way to exploit symmetry planes; cuts can be undone or all reset.
tools.usage: Developer > Add-in Libraries > COMSOL_Multiphysics > planar_cut; Developer > Add-ins > Planar Cut: Plane, Remove side (Downside/Upside), Coordinate (Midpoint/User defined) > Create Cut / Undo Last / Reset

parameters.name: Plane
parameters.description: xy-plane | xz-plane | yz-plane.

parameters.name: Remove side
parameters.description: Downside or Upside.

parameters.name: Coordinate
parameters.description: Midpoint of the geometry extent or user defined.

tools.example: Check valve model symmetric about xz: Planar Cut with Plane = xz, Remove side = Downside, Coordinate = Midpoint, then add Symmetry conditions on the new face.
tools.notes: Remember to apply symmetry boundary conditions on the cut plane in every physics interface.

tools.name: State-Space Controller (add-in)
tools.description: COMSOL Multiphysics add-in that implements full-state feedback u = -Lx for a controllable linear time-invariant system x' = Ax + Bu, y = Cx by pole placement: you enter A, B, C, initial conditions and desired closed-loop poles, and it creates a 0D component with global equations and reports the output variables. The controller output can then drive sources in any physics model.
tools.usage: Developer > Add-in Libraries > COMSOL_Multiphysics > state_space_controller; Developer > Add-ins > State-Space Controller: Dimension, matrices A and C, vector B, initial values, pole locations > Create

parameters.name: Dimension
parameters.description: Size of the state vector.

parameters.name: A, B, C
parameters.description: System matrices (D = 0 assumed).

parameters.name: Poles
parameters.description: Desired closed-loop pole locations in the left half plane.

tools.example: Second-order thermal model with A = [[-1, 1], [0, -2]], B = [0; 1], C = [1, 0]: place poles at -3 and -4, create the controller, and connect its output variable to a heater source in the physics model.
tools.notes: The system must be controllable for pole placement to succeed.

tools.name: Plasma Chemistry (add-in)
tools.description: Plasma Module add-in that builds a complete plasma chemistry (species with preset or user-defined thermodynamic data, electron-impact reactions from cross sections or rate constants, heavy-species and surface reactions) in the Plasma or Plasma, Time Periodic interface from a structured text file with SPECIES, ...REACTIONS blocks. Rate expressions may use TE, NE, TGAS, EN or any plasma.* variable.
tools.usage: Developer > Add-in Libraries > Plasma_Module > plasma_chemistry; Developer > Add-ins > Plasma Chemistry: select the chemistry file and the target plasma interface > create

parameters.name: SPECIES block
parameters.description: PRESETSPECIESDATA or USERDEFINED species properties.

parameters.name: Electron impact / HEAVYSPECIESREACTIONS / surface reaction blocks
parameters.description: Reactions with energies and rate constants or cross sections.

parameters.name: Keywords
parameters.description: TE (eV), NE (1/m^3), TGAS (K), EN (V*m^2); plasma.<var> for model variables.

tools.example:
SPECIES
PRESETSPECIESDATA
Ar = Ar
Ar_1p = Ar
END
% electron impact ionization
e+Ar=>2e+Ar+ ! Ionization 15.7 2.3e-14*TE^0.56*exp(-17.1/TE)
tools.notes: Lines starting with % are comments; every block ends with END.

tools.name: Discrete Fracture Network 2D / 3D (add-in)
tools.description: Porous Media Flow and Subsurface Flow Module add-ins that generate stochastic discrete fracture networks - line fractures in 2D or elliptical disc fractures in 3D - as a geometry part with size, position, orientation (uniform, power law, Fisher) and aperture (including size-proportional) distributions, and add a cubic-law Fracture feature to a new or existing Darcy's Law interface with aperture variables. The network can be regenerated with different statistics for Monte Carlo style studies.
tools.usage: Developer > Add-in Libraries > Porous_Media_Flow_Module (or Subsurface_Flow_Module) > discrete_fracture_network_2d / discrete_fracture_network_3d; Developer > Add-ins > Discrete Fracture Network

parameters.name: Size / position distributions
parameters.description: Uniform random or power law.

parameters.name: Orientation
parameters.description: Fisher distribution with dispersion coefficient K.

parameters.name: Aperture
parameters.description: Distribution or size proportional (a = c*l).

parameters.name: Target component
parameters.description: Existing or new component and Darcy's Law interface.

tools.example: Create a 3D DFN of 200 elliptical fractures with power-law sizes and Fisher orientations in a 100 m rock block, mesh fractures first with triangles, then solve Darcy flow with the generated Fracture feature.
tools.notes: Complex networks may need geometry cleanup or manual meshing; the CAD kernel is recommended for 3D networks.
